### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2R1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.713)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:22954)

**Proposed mechanism:** POGLUT1 (HGNC:22954) —DISRUPTS→ Glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis (GO:0006017); Glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis (GO:0006017) —LEADS_TO→ Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (HP:0003689); Glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis (GO:0006017) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital muscular dystrophy (HP:0001290). Loss-of-function variants in POGLUT1 disrupt glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis, leading to distinct but overlapping muscular dystrophy phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in POGLUT1 with a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in either disease would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if POGLUT1 variants were found to have a frequency >1% in gnomAD in a homozygous state, it would suggest a non-pathogenic role for loss-of-function. _(variant: HGNC:22954)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding that both diseases stem from POGLUT1 dysfunction in glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for both congenital and limb-girdle muscular dystrophies.

#### 2. aortic valve disease 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.427)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1912399)

**Proposed mechanism:** NOTCH1 (HGNC:7941) —DISRUPTS→ NOTCH signaling pathway (GO:0007219); NOTCH signaling pathway (GO:0007219) —LEADS_TO→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); NOTCH signaling pathway (GO:0007219) —LEADS_TO→ cell-cell adhesion (GO:0007155); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Aortic valve disease (HP:0001657); cell-cell adhesion (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Cutis laxa (HP:0000972). Haploinsufficiency of NOTCH1 disrupts the NOTCH signaling pathway, which in turn affects extracellular matrix organization and cell-cell adhesion. Dysregulation of these processes contributes to the phenotypes of both Aortic valve disease and Cutis laxa.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any mutations in NOTCH1 in individuals with either Cutis laxa or Aortic valve disease, or identification of distinct and unrelated causal pathways for each disease. _(variant: rs140003337)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NOTCH1 and downstream pathways in both diseases could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting extracellular matrix integrity and cell adhesion for both conditions.

Loss-of-function variants in NOTCH1 cause Adams-Oliver syndrome 5 by disrupting the Jagged-Notch signaling pathway. Similarly, loss-of-function variants in POGLUT1 disrupt the same Jagged-Notch signaling pathway, leading to the phenotype of MONDO:0014307. The convergence occurs at the level of the shared signaling pathway.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic sequencing reveals that the causal variants in NOTCH1 and POGLUT1 do not lead to functional impairment of the Notch signaling pathway, or if mutations in these genes are found to be common in the healthy population (e.g., gnomAD allele frequency > 0.1%) suggesting they are benign variants. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the Notch signaling pathway in these two diseases, mediated by NOTCH1 and POGLUT1, could inform therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for developmental disorders.

#### 4. familial partial lipodystrophy, Kobberling type  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.399)

Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in NOTCH3 disrupt Golgi apparatus protein modification and trafficking, leading to partial lipodystrophy (MONDO:0012072). The convergence point is the shared disruption of Golgi apparatus function.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that POGLUT1 and NOTCH3 do not converge on common downstream pathways within the Golgi apparatus, or that mutations in one gene do not affect the function of pathways impacted by the other gene. _(variant: None available for the specific pathogenic variants.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of Golgi apparatus dysfunction in these distinct diseases could reveal novel therapeutic targets for interventions aimed at restoring protein modification and trafficking, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 6. lateral meningocele syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.398)

Loss-of-function mutations in POGLUT1 disrupt Golgi protein glycosylation, leading to cerebral calcification. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in NOTCH3 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, resulting in skeletal abnormalities and lateral meningoceles. The convergence occurs at the level of cellular processes involved in matrix homeostasis and protein modification, which are fundamental to both neurodevelopment and skeletal development.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for POGLUT1 and NOTCH3 that do not converge on shared downstream cellular processes or extracellular matrix components. Furthermore, the absence of any known interaction or functional relationship between Golgi glycosylation and Notch signaling in relevant cell types would falsify this hypothesis. The presence of common, highly penetrant variants in gnomAD for either POGLUT1 or NOTCH3 would also weaken the claim of these genes causing rare diseases. _(variant: rs750779849 (POGLUT1 c.1438G>A p.Gly480Arg) has a frequency of 0.00012 in European populations, which is not high enough to falsify pathogenicity.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic underpinnings of POGLUT1 and NOTCH3 related disorders could reveal therapeutic targets that address common pathways, potentially leading to treatments for both conditions. For instance, strategies aimed at restoring extracellular matrix integrity or modulating Golgi function might offer synergistic benefits.
